tossups.text: In a two-part episode of this show entitled "A Long Walk to Pittsburgh," a character is allowed to stay with her Aunt Prudence after her parents move away. The wrestler Vader appeared on an episode of this show, which was set at Pennbrook University during its last two seasons. This show, which was part of ABC's TGIF lineup, included the nerdy character Minkus as well as Angela and Shawn, who had an interracial relationship. A recent spin-off of this show stars Rowan Blanchard as Riley, whose dad is a history teacher at her middle school. For 10 points, name this show that starred William Daniels and Ben Savage as Mr. Feeny and Cory Matthews.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for adrenal cortex hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The adrenal is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in adrenal cortex hormones.

tossups.text: This group's membership was significantly expanded by the addition of a group known as the "A8". This group, which was preceded by the EEC and ECSC, was established via the 1992 Maastricht Treaty. In a move nicknamed "Brexit", the United Kingdom voted to leave this organization in a referendum. The Euro is the official currency of, for 10 points, what organization of European states?
acceptableAnswers: accept answers in any of the other 23 official EU languages

tossups.text: During this president's administration, Coleman Blease read an extremely racist poem on the Senate floor after Jessie de Priest was invited by his wife. Charles Mitchell was blamed by the Pecora Commission during this president's tenure. Thomas Lamont begged this president to not pass a bill that was condemned by Paul Douglas. This president, who killed the Young plan, was petitioned by over 1000 economists to not pass a certain law. Walter Waters led a protest on the Anacostia Flats against this president. This president, who founded the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, had earlier promised voters a "chicken in every pot." This president passed the Smoot-Hawley Tariff and was opposed by the Bonus Army. For 10 points, name this president whose tenure saw the start of the Great Depression.

Achaemenides hitched a ride with this figure, who carries with him household deities called the Penates; this man's enemies included Mezentius and Amata. His mother saves him from Diomedes, but he is wounded in the process, and then saved by Apollo. His father, made lame as a punishment for fathering him, is Anchises. After being visited in a dream by his friend Hector, he flees Troy, and this son of Venus later sails from Carthage despite the appeals of Dido. For 10 points, name this man whose descendant Romulus founded Rome, the title character of an epic poem by Virgil.

This deity gave Lamia removable eyes, and took on the appearance of Artemis to seduce Callisto. This deity transformed into an eagle to abduct both Aegina and the shepherd-boy Ganymede, who became this deity's cupbearer on Mount Olympus. This god's female lovers included Semele and Leto, who gave birth on Delos to this god's children, Artemis and Apollo. For 10 points, name this philandering Greek sky god, the husband of Hera.

In Fortran, subsets of these entities may be obtained by slicing them. Memory-allocating growth factors correspond to the dynamic type of these entities, which may be specified via dope vectors. In C++, strings are represented as these entities containing chars, and these entities can be multidimensional. The list type of these entities do not contain a set number of elements. In Java, these entities are declared by indicating the type of their elements, followed by square brackets. For 10 points, name these data structures in computer science that are analogous to matrices.

This force arises due to the interactions of asperities[as-PAIR-uh-teez]. Amontons' second law notes thatthe size of this force isn't affected by the surface area of contact. Formulas involving this force include mu [mew], this force's coefficient, which can be changed by adding or removing lubricants. There are static and kinetic types of, for ten points, what force that opposes motion and, thus, slows down objects that are sliding on a surface?

One character created by this author flies to Nice to stay with her father's first wife Katya, then becomes the mistress of academic Bernard Chaballier. The protagonist of another of her novels is a businessman who discovers that his son Terry is gay and one day finds a corpse on his farm. This creator of Mehring wrote a novel that ends with Bam having lost his gun and bakkie and Maureen chasing after a helicopter. In that book by this author of The Conservationist, a civil war forces the Smales family to flee to their servant's village from Johannesburg. For 10 points, identify this South African author of Burger's Daughter and July's People.

Mutation in a protein responsible for processing these proteins causes restrictive dermopathy in infants; that protein is the matrix metalloproteinase ZMPSTE24. An abnormal form of these proteins retains the farnesyl group on its C-terminus after processing. One isoform of these proteins interacts with emerin, mutations in which cause Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy. The A and C types of these proteins are alternatively spliced from the same gene. Activation of a cryptic splice site at glycine-608 on one of these proteins is a cause of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria. These proteins' rod domains bind to S/MAR regions, which contain AT-rich patches. These proteins are phosphorylated by MPF during the cell cycle in order to disassemble a certain organelle. For 10 points, name these intermediate filaments that form a meshwork on the inner surface of the nucleus.

One of these objects made out of hair in Inca myth was called Tequendama. In Islam, one of these objects as narrow as a hair and as sharp as a sword is called the as-Sirat. In Zoroastrianism, Rashnu guards one of these objects called Chinvat. A group of bears and monkeys throws rocks into a sea to create one of these structures in the Ramayana. Heimdallr guards the entrance to one of these structures made out of rainbows that leads to Asgard. For 10 points, name these structures that in several myth systems must be traversed to reach other realms.

This region's city of Birobidzhan ["bee-ROH-beed-jahn"] is the capital of the world's only Jewish administrative division. Nerpa seals are endemic to a body of water in this region also home to the Buryat people. A peninsula in this region contains the Valley of Geysers and encloses the Sea of Okhotsk ["oh-KOTSK"]. This region is crossed by a namesake railway whose eastern terminus is in Vladivostok. This region's city of Irkutsk sits near the deepest lake in the world. Lake Baikal is in, for 10 points, what vast region of Russia east of the Ural Mountains?
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Kamchatka Peninsula during the third line

tossups.text: Some speakers of this language add the consonant 'r' to the end of syllables in a process called erhua. This language contains measure words such as "ge" and "zhi", which are used to quantify nouns. During the 20th century, some characters used to write this language were simplified, though the traditional forms are still used in Taiwan. For 10 points, name this language spoken in Beijing.

Archduke Joseph Karl Ludwig established a small colony for this ethnic group on his Alcsúth ("ALL-choot") estate. Balance between užo ("oo-ZHO") and marime was integral to this ethnic group's kris courts, where the Vlax dialect was mostly spoken. Members of this ethnic group were labeled "New Citizens" by Maria Theresa, who later forced them to marry gadjos. A subgroup of this ethnicity became associated with copper smithing, from which the name kalderash originated. Members of this ethnic group were forced to wear an inverted brown triangle during the Porajmos ("po-RYE-mohs"). Czechoslovakia's Chanov housing projects were intended as ghettos for these people, whose ethnic flag features the Dharmachakra wheel. For 10 points, name this Indo-Aryan ethnic group who often traveled in wagons as nomads.
acceptableAnswers: accept specific subgroups such as Sinti
Gypsies by asking “that term is considered a slur
what is an endonym of the group?”

tossups.text: An unusual type of this plant, Pereskia, can produce rose-like flowers. This plant is the habitat for cochineals [kah-chih-neels], insects that are harvested to produce a deep red dye. These succulent plants have areoles, small, spiny bumps that defend the plant's stem. The saguaro [sah-WAHR-oh] is a giant example of this plant found in Sonora and Arizona. For 10 points, name this plant that typically has excellent water storage abilities to survive in the desert.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for phagocytes and macrophages. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this phagocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The phagocyte is a key component of the Immune system, involved in phagocytes and macrophages.

tossups.text: In this novel's frame story, Zillah puts the narrator in an oak closet to sleep, where he is frightened by a spirit. A man in this novel marries and abuses Isabella Linton and cheats Hareton Earnshaw out of his inheritence. While visiting this novel's title house near Thrushcross Grange, Lockwood is disturbed by the ghost of his landlord's lost love, Catherine. For 10 points, name this novel in which Heathcliff gets revenge on the inhabitants of the title house, written by Emily Bront¨e.

Fossils from this geologic period are found in the Chinle Formation in Arizona. The notable non-dinosaur Lystrosaurus was a ubiquitous herbivore during the early part of this period and may have been fed on by Cynognathus. Sauropterygians were marine reptiles that first evolved during this period, which also saw the first ichthyosaurs. Synapsids and mammal-like reptiles declined in importance during this period, which was marked by the diversification of diapsid reptiles and saw the first ornithischians and theropods. This period was directly preceded by the eruption of the Siberian Traps, which may have caused the great extinction at the end of the Permian. For 10 points, name this first period of the Mesozoic Era, during which dinosaurs evolved.

This activity was used to determine succession to the thrones of Ophion and Eurynome. One instance of this activity has been viewed as either the duty of a Frazerian year-king or the cruel whim of a ruler who also buried his daughter Alope ("AL-uh-pee") alive for having a son with Poseidon. By one account, this activity was invented by the androgynous Palaestra, who names spaces where it occurred. Passers-by were challenged to this activity and then killed by Cercyon ("SIR-see-on"), who was later killed by Theseus. Antaeus, a son of Gaia, was undefeated in this activity because he was invincible while he touched his mother, but was crushed to death by Heracles. For 10 points, name this sport in which participants attempt to grapple the other to the ground.

Idris Bitlisi mobilized the Kurds under this man's rule, and he appointed Al Asraf Bey to govern another conquered territory. He ordered the deaths of the Turkish Kizilbash in order to hurt a Safavid rival, whom he would eventually defeat after taking Amid uncontested. He achieved victories in the Battles of Radinayah and Marj Dabiq, and after he defeated Shah Ismail in the Battle of Chaldiran, he conquered the Mamluks. For 10 points, name this Ottoman emperor, the son of Bayezid II who added Syria and Egypt to the empire and fathered Suleiman the Magnificent.

parts.text: Name this Impressionist whose homoerotic themes in paintings such as Le Pont de l'Europe are analyzed in Norma Broude's essay "Outing Impressionism." A bottle of red wine sits on the far right of a painting by this artist which depicts three shirtless men.

Caillebotte's The Floor Scrapers was rejected from the 1875 iteration of this event due to its "vulgar" depiction of those shirtless men. This biennial event was the premier art exhibition in Paris throughout the 1800s.

Caillebotte himself is portrayed sitting backwards in this painting set at a restaurant owned by Alphonse Fournaise. This painting portrays the artist's future wife Aline Charigot playing with a dog on a white tablecloth.
acceptableAnswers: The Luncheon of the Boating Party

bonuses.leadin: This artist's photographic realism is discussed in a 1987 essay by Peter Galassi which claims he traced his paintings and is titled after this artist's "space." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with capillary exchange.
What is the main function of the aorta in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to capillary exchange.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this eastern European region which, in 2008, declared itself an independent country with capital Pristina.
Kosovo seceeded from this nation with capital Belgrade. In 2006, the nation of Montenegro declared itself independent from this country.

Serbia and Montenegro was the final remnant of this eastern European Communist union, not allied with the Soviet Union that formed after World War II. In 1991, it dissolved into Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia, Serbia and Montenegro, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

bonuses.leadin: A 1999 war in this region began after aggression from Slobodan Milosevic, who had earlier sparked war in Bosnia. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Identify this Confederate general, who was promoted to that rank after a battle that felled Albert Sidney Johnston and who famously didn't pursue defeated Union troops after a victory at Chickamauga.
Name that Tennessee-fought battle where Johnston died, where Bragg attacked the Hornet's Nest, and where Lew Wallace misinterpreted an order from Grant, missing the fighting.

During Bragg's invasion of this state, one wing of Bragg's army under Leonidas Polk beat the Union at the Battle of Perrysville, but despite pleas to fight Buell in this state, Bragg promptly retreated.

bonuses.leadin: Legend has it that he had a written dispute with himself when he served as post quartermaster and company commander concurrently. For 10 points each:

parts.text: When Odysseus returns from his voyage, he first slays this young suitor, who attempted to have Telemachus killed.
This wife of Odysseus is forever faithful to her husband, and yanks the suitors along by weaving and unweaving on her large loom.
This beautiful nymph falls in love with Odysseus after he lands on her island of Ogygia. Hermes finally convinces her to let him go after seven years.

bonuses.leadin: Name these characters from Homer's Odyssey, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this bad-tempered lightning god for whom the Sons of Ivaldi created the hammer Mjolnir [mee-YOLL-neer]. During Ragnar¨ok, the Norse apocalypse, this god and the great serpent Jormungandr [YOR-mun-gon-dur] will kill each other in battle.
This queen of the Vanir, the Norse nature gods, owned a magical cloak made of falcon feathers which she could use to fly. She claimed half the souls of dead warriors for her mead-hall, F´olkvangr.
This Norse goddess used her mystical spinning wheel to create the clouds. This wife of Odin is the goddess of both family life and clairvoyance.

bonuses.leadin: Many of the Norse gods owned magical objects. For example, this god's wife, Sif, possessed a golden cap made by the dwarven Sons of Ivaldi. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this phenomenon that explains how a pole traveling near the speed of light can fit in a barn that is normally too small to completely contain it.
Length contraction and time dilation are two consequences of this theory proposed by Albert Einstein, which rests on the assumptions of a constant speed of light and no preferred reference frame.

With Alexander Rankine, this physicist showed that length contraction does not occur in the rest reference frame. Between 1901 and 1903, he and H.R. Noble found that Earth did not move relative to the ether.

bonuses.leadin: This phenomenon occurs in the resting frame in Bell's spaceship paradox, explaining why the string breaks. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this irrational number about equal to 2.71828.
Jacob Bernoulli discovered e by studying the compound form of this concept, the money earned by lending money to a borrower.

e can also be calculated by taking this process, as x approaches infinity, of the quantity 1 + 1 over x, quantity raised to the x power. In the 19th century, Cauchy [koh-shee] formalized this calculus operation in terms of variables often labeled epsilon and delta.

bonuses.leadin: The natural log of this number is equal to 1, because this number is the base of the natural logarithm. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this movement exemplified by poems like "In a Station of the Metro."
This friend of H.D. composed the short poem "In a Station of the Metro" and published the three rules of Imagism in the essay "A Retrospect." This poet failed to complete the epic poem The Cantos.

H.D. implores this entity to "hurl your green over us, / cover us with your pools of fir" in the poem "Oread"("oh-REE-add"). H.D. included five flower poems in a collection titled for a garden of this entity.

bonuses.leadin: H.D. contributed to a list of three rules of this movement, which advocates for "no superfluous words" and the "direct treatment of the thing." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these processes that involve repeated pair production and bremsstrahlung ("BREM-sh'trah-lung"). The width and length of these processes is characterized by the Moliere radius and radiation depth, respectively.

These detectors totally absorb particle showers in order to determine the energy and position of the incident particle. These detectors are classified as hadronic or electromagnetic based upon the type of particle they measure.

Calorimeters can measure values in the billions for this SI unit of energy in particle physics, which is equal to roughly 1.6 times 10 to the negative 19 joules. The Tevatron is named for being able to accelerate particles up to about 1 trillion of these units.

bonuses.leadin: A simple analytic model of these processes that describes their longitudinal development was developed by Heitler. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these mythological beings generally imagined with the torso of a woman and the tail of a fish.
These Celtic maidens of the sea often marry the men who steal their seal skins, at least until they can return to the water.
These Japanese "mermaids" are often depicted as hideous creatures, but those who catch and eat them are said to have eternal youth and a long life.

bonuses.leadin: These creatures are known as ceasg in Scotland, rusalkas in Eastern Europe, and maneli in Ancient Persia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This city on the Arno river is the capital of Tuscany, and features the large-domed Duomo designed by Brunelleschi. It was an important Renaissance city under the Medicis.
This northwestern city in Sicily, the largest on that island, celebrates Saint Rosalia's Day every July 15.
This city is close to the Adriatic Sea, and was the last capital of the Western Roman Empire.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about Italian cities for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this economic and game theory concept where all forces and agents are in balanced unchanging positions.

The most famous equilibrium, where no player can benefit from changing their strategy, was formulated by this American mathematician, whose battles with schizophrenia were dramatized in A Beautiful Mind.
The only Nash equilibrium in this strategic game is for both namesake players to defect, instead of staying silent in an attempt to get a reduced sentence.

bonuses.leadin: It includes Markov-perfect, Mertens-stable, correlative, and competitive varieties. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Not to be confused with Saturnalia, this festival took place in mid-February and featured the sacrifice of a goat and a dog, after which the priests would run through town and slap people with the skin of the goat.
This man was the chief religious officer of the state. He took over cultic responsibilities originally held by the king, and his title later became an unofficial title of the Catholic Pope.
This other Roman festival was held on May 9, 11, and 13 and was designed to pacify the vengeful ghosts of the dead. The pater familias would throw beans to keep the ghosts at bay.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about religion in ancient Rome. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel which follows the Buendia family over seven generations as they inhabit the town of Macondo.
acceptableAnswers: The One Hundred Years of Solitude

parts.text: This author used magic realism in One Hundred Years of Solitude and also wrote Love in the Time of Cholera.
Garcia Marquez also wrote this fictionalized account of the dying days of Simon Bolivar.

bonuses.leadin: One character in this work has 17 sons by 17 different women. For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this character who comes to Earth after leaving asteroid B-612. After landing in the Sahara Desert, he talks to a fox and meets a pilot who has crash-landed in the desert.
Eventually, the Little Prince is killed by one of these animals.

On the Prince's home asteroid, there are three volcanoes, several plants, and this thing, which the Prince falls in love with. The Prince thinks this thing is unique to his asteroid until he comes to Earth and sees how common it is.

bonuses.leadin: This character has golden hair and refuses to directly answer questions. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these events hosted by a sea god at Hlesey (L'YES-ay"). Another one of these events is the setting of the Lokasenna("LOH-kah-sen-uh"), in which Loki insults the attendants and kills the servant Fimafeng ("FEE-mah-feng").
acceptableAnswers: answers that describe a meal hosted by Aegir

parts.text: In the Skáldskaparmál("SKAL-skap-ur-mall"), Aegir is told about how the gods started to age when the kidnapping of Idunn ("EE-thohn") deprived them of these fruits. Hippomenes ("hih-PAH-muh-neez") threw these fruits on the ground to distract Atalanta in a footrace.
The Skáldskaparmál also tells the story of these two giantesses with rhyming names, who ran a mill to create gold for King Fróði ("FROH-thee"), and later salt for the sea-king Mysing. Name either.

bonuses.leadin: The Hymiskviða("HOO-may-SKVEE-thuh") follows the Aesir's ("acer's") quest to find a kettle large enough to be used at one of these events, which they eventually obtain from Hymir ("HOO-mair"). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this leader of the First Serbian Uprising against the Ottomans, who became the founder of modern Serbia.

An inciting factor in the First Serbian Uprising was the Slaughter of the Dukes, in which dahijas massacred nobles with this title found in many Slavic languages. Alexander of Battenberg held this title as prince of Bulgaria.
The dahijas who committed the Slaughter of the Dukes were renegade members of this Ottoman infantry force, which was dissolved in the Auspicious Incident.
